Never trust AI blindly just because it sounds confident.
While researching veganism, I got a statistic from Claude that sounded completely believable. Since a few other stats it gave me were accurate, I trusted this one too without double-checking.

Big mistake.

The moment I asked for the source, I realized it wasn’t actually pulled from a solid reference, it was an inferred answer presented like a fact.
That was my wake-up call.
AI tools can sound incredibly convincing, even when they’re wrong. Always ask for the source, verify the data, and fact-check before using any information in your content, research, or decisions.
Confidence does not equal accuracy.

→ On iPhone, ChatGPT can sit inside Siri through Apple Intelligence. Sign in once and Siri hands your hardest questions straight to ChatGPT.

→ There’s an apps and connectors option in the sidebar that lets you plug your tools directly into your chats.

→ Data controls let you turn off “improve the model for everyone” so your conversations stop training it. And if all this memory talk freaked you out a little, there’s a temporary chat option that remembers nothing at all.

These settings are sitting inside your app right now and almost nobody has opened that tab.
